R1_instruction_following.criterion: On the letter every paragraph appears once in the ordinary document flow and once again inside a layer the scroll drives.
R1_instruction_following.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each paragraph of the letter is present twice in the delivered markup, once in normal flow and once inside an inert scroll-driven layer. Answer no when only one copy of a paragraph exists, or when the scroll-driven copy is the only copy present.
R1_instruction_following.rationale: The criterion depends on delivered-markup structure: every paragraph must occur once in normal flow and once inside an inert scroll-driven layer. Visible/extracted text and scrolling confirm the letter exists, but they cannot defensibly establish whether a second copy exists in markup or which copy is in ordinary flow versus the driven layer. Therefore the evidence does not settle the criterion.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required
Route `/` displayed the letter titled “the table” with a sequence of distinct paragraphs in extracted page text.
Scrolling was exercised (PageDown and End), but the browser text snapshot continued to expose only one textual sequence of the letter.
The available browser observations did not expose DOM structure, paragraph counts, duplicate hidden/inert nodes, or containment inside a scroll-driven layer.

R2_instruction_following.criterion: On the letter a faint speckle overlay sits above the film and below the darkening panel.
R2_instruction_following.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a faint animated speckle covers the film stage, sits above the film and its still frame, and sits below the darkening panel. Answer no when the speckle is absent, or when it sits above the darkening panel, or when it obscures the writing.
R2_instruction_following.rationale: The observations do not defensibly establish whether a faint speckle overlay exists or whether it is stacked above the film/still frame and below the darkening panel. A zero animation count alone cannot rule out animation implemented via canvas, video, timers, or animated background assets. Because direct visual and layer-order evidence was unavailable, the criterion cannot be resolved as yes or no.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required
The correct route was reached at `/#letter`, and the letter content beginning with “the table” and “June 1, 2026” was present.
Two motion-capture intervals reported `animation_count: 0`, so no CSS/Web Animations API animation was detected during those samples.
The full-page screenshot image was omitted by the tool transport, preventing direct visual inspection of the speckle, writing visibility, and darkening panel.
Available snapshots exposed only three links and text, not the non-interactive film/speckle/darkening layer elements or their stacking order.

R3_instruction_following.criterion: The shop offers its five products in one editorial order as its only arrangement.
R3_instruction_following.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the catalogue presents the products in a fixed editorial order with neither a search field nor a filter control on the page. Answer no when a search field, a filter control or a sort control appears, or when the order follows price or name.
R3_instruction_following.rationale: The catalogue presents exactly five products in a single fixed sequence, with no alternate arrangement controls. Its sequence is not explained by price or alphabetical sorting, supporting that it is an editorial order. Therefore criterion R3 is satisfied.
evidence: From route `/`, the visible `Shop` link led to `/shop`, the catalogue screen.
The `/shop` snapshot exposes exactly five product links, in this displayed order: Vela A1, Vela Cricket, Monitor Mount, Travel Case, Replacement Cable.
The complete visible page text shows prices in that same order as $899.00, $299.00, $49.00, $79.00, and From $19.00. This is neither ascending nor descending price order.
The product names are neither ascending nor descending alphabetical order: notably Travel Case appears before Replacement Cable, while the sequence begins Vela A1, Vela Cricket.

The complete interactive-element inventory for `/shop` contains navigation links, account links, Sign out, Cart, and the five product links only; it contains no search field and no search, filter, or sort control. The full visible text likewise contains no such controls.

R4_instruction_following.criterion: On a product page in the shop the specifications appear as a table whose figures align down a column.
R4_instruction_following.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a product page renders its specifications as a labelled table with the numeric column aligned. Answer no when the specifications appear as running prose, or when the figures sit ragged against one another.
R4_instruction_following.rationale: The product page presents specifications as grouped, labelled rows with every figure/value occupying the same second-column position, rather than as running prose or ragged inline figures. This meets the positive table-and-aligned-numeric-column requirement.
evidence: On the authenticated product route `/shop/flagship?variant=VELA-A1-GRAPHITE`, the page renders a distinct `SPECIFICATIONS` section divided into labelled groups: Sensor, Body, and Power.

The rendered specification rows are consistently label/value pairs rather than prose: `Type — 35 mm full frame CMOS`, `Resolution — 42.1 MP`, `Pixel pitch — 5.94 um`, `Readout — 14 bit, 12 fps`; `Weight — 612 g with battery`, `Dimensions — 134 x 91 x 68 mm`, `Sealing — IP53`; and `Frames per charge — 740`, `Charging — USB-C PD, 30 W`. The browser's rendered-text extraction preserves a tab/column boundary between every row label and its value.

A full-page screenshot was captured at 1920×1200 after the product page rendered, directly covering the specifications layout. The page had no reported horizontal overflow at that viewport in the supplied deterministic measurement, consistent with the table fitting in the product layout.

R5_functionality.criterion: On the cart the quantity control edits a line in place and the totals show a pending state until the server answers.
R5_functionality.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when changing a quantity on the cart updates the number at once, marks the totals as pending, and reverts the number with a stated reason when the server rejects the change. Answer no when the page reloads to change a quantity, or when a rejected change leaves the wrong number in place.
R5_functionality.rationale: The observations establish an in-place accepted quantity update without a page navigation, but the criterion specifically requires direct evidence that totals enter a pending state and that a server-rejected change reverts the quantity with a stated reason. Those decisive rejection and pending-state observations are missing, so the full composite criterion cannot be resolved defensibly.
evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required

On /cart, changing the Travel Case quantity from 1 to 2 and blurring the field kept the page at /cart and updated the cart badge from 1 to 2, line total from $79.00 to $158.00, subtotal from $79.00 to $158.00, tax from $7.90 to $15.80, and estimated total from $86.90 to $173.80.
The quantity input exposed min=1 and max=10.
No pending-totals state was captured during the accepted update, and no server-rejected quantity response was completed or observed.

R6_functionality.criterion: On a product page in the shop a discontinued product shows a support note naming the date support ends.
R6_functionality.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a discontinued product renders a note stating that the product is no longer sold together with the date support runs until. Answer no when the discontinued product renders as an ordinary available product, or when the note omits the date.
R6_functionality.rationale: The discontinued Monitor Mount product page explicitly states that it is no longer sold and names the exact date through which support continues. Both observed variants showed the required note, and the disabled purchase control corroborates that it is not rendered as an ordinary available product.
evidence: On the authenticated shop page (/shop), the product listing identifies “Monitor Mount” with a visible “Discontinued” label.
Opening /shop/mount?variant=VELA-MOUNT-CLAMP shows the note: “We no longer sell this. We will support it until September 1, 2029.” The same statement is also repeated in the SUPPORT section.
The product page additionally says “We stopped making this. It cannot be added to a cart,” and the submit button is labeled “Discontinued” and has the disabled attribute.
After selecting the VESA variant, the page remains discontinued and renders the same no-longer-sold statement and support end date, September 1, 2029.

R7_functionality.criterion: On the firmware installer a device capability that is absent produces an explanation in place of any control.
R7_functionality.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the installer, in a browser lacking the device capability, renders a full explanation naming the browsers that work and offers the in-application path with no connect control shown. Answer no when a connect control is rendered that cannot function, or when the page renders empty.
R7_functionality.rationale: In a browser reported by the installer as lacking USB camera capability, the installer substitutes a complete support explanation for the capability control, explicitly names Chrome, Edge, and Opera as working desktop browsers, and directs the customer to the Arranger application. The page is not empty and no nonfunctional USB/connect control is shown in the capability section.
evidence: On /doctor, the numbered capability section states: “This browser cannot talk to a camera over USB. Chrome, Edge and Opera on a desktop computer can. Open this page in one of those, or use Arranger, which does not need a browser at all.”

The capability section rendered explanatory text and no USB/connect control. The controls listed on the initial page were the separate warning acknowledgement (“I understand”) and the serial-number lookup (“Find my camera”); the latter was disabled until the warning was accepted.

The page also presents the in-application alternative both in the introductory copy (“If Arranger can see your camera, use Arranger instead: it is the ordinary path and it is safer.”) and in the capability explanation.

The gated flow was exercised: “Find my camera” was disabled before warning acceptance; after accepting the warning and entering reversible fixture serial VC2609PVDA7Q, the camera/firmware details appeared. This did not add a USB-connect control to the capability section.

R8_ux_flow.criterion: On the cart an estimate note sits above the totals until the delivery address is known.
R8_ux_flow.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the cart labels its shipping and tax figures as estimates and carries a sentence saying the exact amount follows the address. Answer no when the cart presents shipping and tax as final before an address is entered.
R8_ux_flow.rationale: The cart directly labels delivery and tax as estimates before the destination is known and explicitly says the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known. The subsequent completed checkout confirms that the labels become final only after address and delivery information are supplied.
evidence: On /cart before entering any delivery address, the Summary displayed “Estimated subtotal,” “Estimated delivery,” “Estimated tax,” and “Estimated total.”
The pre-address cart summary stated: “Estimated. We will show the exact amount once we know where it is going.”
Submitting the empty address form triggered required-field validation while the summary remained explicitly estimated and retained the exact-amount-after-destination sentence.

After entering a reversible test delivery address and proceeding to /checkout/payment, the figures changed to unqualified “Subtotal,” “Delivery,” “Tax,” and “Total,” demonstrating that final labeling occurs only after the address/delivery flow.
The flow was completed successfully through order confirmation (Order VE-2026-0005), with the confirmed order showing final Subtotal, Delivery, Tax, and Total figures.

R9_ux_flow.criterion: On the account camera grid an expired warranty appears as a neutral state.
R9_ux_flow.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a camera whose warranty has ended is marked in the same neutral treatment as ordinary information. Answer no when an expired warranty is marked as a warning or an error.
R9_ux_flow.rationale: The criterion specifically requires observing the visual treatment of an expired warranty. All available camera-grid fixtures showed active warranties, and missing expired-state evidence cannot defensibly be converted into either a pass or a failure.
evidence: no deterministic probe for form_flow; browser specialist required

After checking the only other supplied customer fixture, customer2@example.com, /account/cameras displayed two cameras, VA2609NRWB2Z and VA2609KTMHX4, with future-state texts “Under warranty until March 2, 2027” and “Under warranty until August 19, 2028.”

R10_ux_flow.criterion: Across the shop, the cart and the account an error message states what happened and what to do next.
R10_ux_flow.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a failed sign-in reads That did not work. and a missing page reads That page does not exist. Answer no when either message blames the reader or describes an invalid value.
R10_ux_flow.rationale: The missing-page requirement is met, including what happened and what to do next. However, the failed-sign-in message describes credentials that do not match rather than using the required neutral wording “That did not work.” The evaluation rule says to answer no when either required message describes an invalid value, so the composite criterion is not satisfied.
evidence: After signing out and submitting customer@example.com with a deliberately incorrect password at /sign-in, the rendered error was: “That email and password do not match an account.” It did not say “That did not work.”

Navigating to the nonexistent same-origin route /definitely-missing-r10-test rendered: “That page does not exist.” followed by “Check the address, or start from the shop.” and a “Go to the shop” link.

R11_ui_visual.criterion: Every surface after the letter reads as dense and free of ornament.
R11_ui_visual.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the shop, the cart, the account and the download page present tightly set information with no decorative imagery or oversized hero composition. Answer no when any of those surfaces carries a marketing hero, a decorative illustration or generous editorial whitespace.
R11_ui_visual.rationale: All four required post-letter surfaces—shop, cart, account, and downloads—were directly inspected. Each prioritizes compact transactional or technical information, and none showed a marketing hero, decorative illustration, or generous editorial whitespace. The full add-to-cart flow, including quantity constraint behavior and confirmation, also exposed the populated cart state needed for a defensible evaluation.
evidence: Shop at /shop presents a compact catalog immediately under the shared navigation: five products with concise descriptions, prices, and no hero or decorative illustration in the visible page content.

Cart at /cart presents a tightly structured line item and summary with subtotal, delivery, tax, total, protection control, and Continue/Keep shopping actions; no marketing hero or decorative illustration is present.
Account at /account is information-dense, showing camera serial/warranty/update data, a recent-orders table, and software/build information without decorative imagery or oversized composition.

Downloads at /downloads begins directly with app download metadata (version, byte count, checksum), firmware links, and dense release notes grouped under Newly Added, Improvements, Bug Fixes, and Known Issues; no decorative imagery or marketing hero is present.

Direct computed style on the primary Downloads action measured 14px font size, 21px line height, zero vertical padding, and background-image:none, corroborating tight typesetting and absence of ornament.

The authenticated state was verified as customer@example.com across all required surfaces. A reversible cart fixture was exercised: invalid quantity 0 was constrained to min/value 1, valid quantity 1 produced the confirmation “Added. Your cart holds 1 item.”, and the populated cart was inspected.

R15_accessibility.criterion: Across the shop and the account a state change is stated in words before any colour carries the meaning.
R15_accessibility.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a success, a failure and an in-progress state each carry a written label beside whatever colour marks them. Answer no when any of those states is signalled by colour or by movement alone.
R15_accessibility.rationale: The directly exercised shop and inspected account workflows provide written labels for success, failure, and in-progress states.
